children: While Treasury yields have fallen, it doesn't mean fiscal risks have diminished, analysts at Capital Economics write. If the 10-year yield remains around its current level, it will still be around 70 basis points higher than the Congressional Budget Office assumed in February. "If yields do fall further, for instance due to a slowdown in growth or, worse, a recession related to the bursting of the AI bubble, then the loss in government revenues and impact of automatic stabilisers would probably still leave debt dynamics worse off," analysts say. The 10-year Treasury yield hovered around 4.986%, after falling below 5% for the first time in a month on Thursday.(jessica.coacci@wsj.com)
